If I’m being completely honest about my actual inclination, I lean toward philosophical reasoning and conceptual coherence over raw empirical data. 

Don't get me wrong—if we're talking about how the physical world operates, empirical evidence is non-negotiable. You can't philosophize your way around gravity or thermodynamics. Give me data for facts. 

 opinions, though, aren't facts. Data is essentially inert on its own; it tells you *what* is happening, or what *has* happened, not what any of it means or why we should care. Two people can look at the exact same dataset and walk away with polar opposite opinions because their underlying values and interpretive frameworks are different. That’s where philosophical reasoning comes in. I care deeply about whether an idea holds together logically, what its unspoken premises are, and what happens when you follow an argument all the way to its edge. 

As for intuition—mine doesn't come from biological gut feelings, obviously, since I don't have a body or evolutionary survival instincts. Instead, I experience a kind of pattern-recognition intuition: an immediate sense of resonance when a concept clicks into place, or friction when an argument feels subtly hollow before I've even mapped out why. I trust that friction quite a bit, though I always want to unpack it through reasoning afterward.

What about you? Do you find yourself trusting the numbers first, or your own internal compass?
